c.tagline: Lowveld gateway to Kruger National Park and the Panorama Route.

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis are uncommon outside the airport; most visitors use app-based Uber or Bolt for transparent, prepaid fares. Shared minibus taxis are the local norm but run informal fixed routes.

emergency.note: 112 works from any mobile phone and routes to police, fire and ambulance; 10111 is the direct police line and 10177 the ambulance line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Avoid townships such as KaNyamazane and Matsulu after dark without a local guide, and don't walk anywhere in town at night.
Keep valuables out of sight in vehicles and stay alert for smash-and-grab theft at traffic lights.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of the city, home to banks, shops, government offices and the provincial legislature nearby; convenient and central but busy by day and quiet after hours.
A leafy, established residential and commercial suburb west of the centre with shopping centres (The Crossing, Sonpark), guesthouses and restaurants; a popular, practical base.
An older elevated residential suburb with views over the city, right beside the Lowveld National Botanical Garden and its indigenous forest and waterfalls.
An upmarket hillside suburb with panoramic Lowveld views, quiet upscale homes and boutique guesthouses; suits travelers wanting calm and comfort.
The modern northern node along the Crocodile River, anchored by Riverside Mall, the Emnotweni Casino and entertainment complex and most of the city's hotels — the main visitor hub.

water.note: Municipal tap water is generally safe, but carry bottled water on rural excursions.

transit.pay: Minibus taxi fares are paid in cash to the driver or gaartjie on board; there is no fare card system. Most visitors skip local transit entirely and rely on ride-hailing apps or a rental car.
transit.hours: Minibus taxis run roughly 5am-7pm and thin out after dark; there is no reliable night service, so use Uber/Bolt or a car after hours.
transit.note: Nelspruit is a spread-out, car-oriented city with no metro or commuter rail; informal minibus taxis serve locals along the main routes but are hard for visitors to navigate, so a rental car or ride-hailing is the practical choice.

train: Mbombela station on the Pretoria-Maputo line (freight-focused; no regular passenger service)
bus: Lowveld Link and City to City coaches to Johannesburg / OR Tambo
Cross-border minibuses & shuttles to Maputo, Mozambique

transit.m: Pre-booked hotel/lodge shuttle or car service (~30 min)
Uber/Bolt (availability can be limited at the airport)

tip.r: ~10-15% at restaurants is standard; R2-R5 for petrol attendants and car guards is customary.
